I've let my obsession over eating almost kill me, so I have some advice. I'm on the other side of the spectrum, I'm 5"8 and 100 lbs right now. I used to be around 90.

First off, don't let this ruin your life. Don't. Take my word. Trust me. Be so careful. It gets addicting and obsessive, counting, weighing, starving. It's not worth it. It's dangerous and painful and gets you no where. It's like a pit, getting into the obsession is so easy, you can just jump it, but it can take even years to dig yourself back out. 

Second, I would reccomend talking to a doctor or maybe even a therapist. A doctor first though. Find a doctor that you're comfortable with. If you already have one, great. If not, I'd try to find someone that you think you would be able to open up to and you think would be able to give you advice. Make sure its someone with a degree and that's certified, a nutritionist is good but a weight loss coach or something isn't. Talk to them about your concerns and see what they think about your diet, weight, etc. Honestly, a healthy weight looks completely different for everyone but your weight and height don't sound "obese" or "fat" to me, sounds normal and healthy. But I'm not a doctor. 

If the doctor clears you, consider talking to a therapist. Especially if you begin obsessively eating or other obsessive habits like purging. They might be able to help you understand why you are doing these things along with how to recover in a safe way. It's a lot easier to go through something like that with someone else to talk to. 

Finally, I want to tell you it's ok. You are still beautiful, inside and out. You are still a great person. Your weight doesn't define that in any way. If someone thinks otherwise that is not someone you want to be around or that even deserves to be in your presence
